html:
The Indian National Army was a force of Indian soldiers that fought beside Japan against the British in the Second World War. It lost every battle and helped end British rule.

It was first raised in 1942 from Indian prisoners taken when Singapore fell to Japan. In 1943 Subhas Chandra Bose, who had escaped from India and reached Asia by submarine, took command. He declared a Provisional Government of Free India and recruited among Indian workers and traders in Malaya and Burma. The army reached about 40,000, with a women's regiment named after the Rani of Jhansi. Its cry was "Chalo Delhi", on to Delhi.

In 1944 it marched with the Japanese into India at Imphal and Kohima. The attack failed, and thousands died of hunger and disease in the retreat through Burma. Bose died after an air crash in August 1945.

The British then put three officers, a Hindu, a Muslim and a Sikh, on trial for treason at the Red Fort. India rose in their defence; Nehru put on his lawyer's gown for the first time in decades. They were convicted and at once set free. In February 1946 sailors of the Indian navy mutinied in Bombay. The British could no longer count on the Indian armed forces.
sum: The Indian National Army was a force of Indian soldiers that fought beside Japan against the British in the Second World War. It lost every battle and helped end British rule.
